purpose: Keep Plantago evidence species-resolved. Presence of one Plantago species in one tortoise taxon must not be converted into genus-wide safety, captive frequency, or unlimited feeding guidance.

evidence.plant_part: dietary plant fragments / field feeding ecology record
evidence.supports: P. amplexicaulis was documented in the diet of wild T. g. graeca in Morocco.
evidence.does_not_support: Direct T. g. ibera evidence; safety of all Plantago spp.; captive diet percentage, staple status, daily feeding, or unlimited feeding.

evidence.supports: P. lanceolata was directly reported among plants consumed by T. h. boettgeri in the Bulgarian field study.
evidence.does_not_support: P. lanceolata as direct T. g. ibera evidence or genus-wide Plantago safety.

evidence.supports: Independent field observation of T. h. hermanni feeding on P. lanceolata.
evidence.does_not_support: Direct evidence for T. g. ibera, genus-wide Plantago feeding rules, or captive frequency.

evidence.study_type: controlled UV exposure study with described captive diet
evidence.supports: P. lanceolata was one component of the diet used for Hermann's tortoises during the study.
evidence.does_not_support: A feeding trial establishing P. lanceolata safety, optimal proportion, or a T. g. ibera recommendation.

canonical_interpretation.current_master_identity: Retain Plantago spp. unless a particular specimen/product is identified to species.
canonical_interpretation.applicability: Related T. graeca subspecies plus related Testudo species; no exact T. g. ibera Plantago species record verified in this pass.
canonical_interpretation.verdict_guardrail: Do not upgrade the public Plantago master solely because P. amplexicaulis or P. lanceolata appears in another population/species. Do not infer that every Plantago species is interchangeable.
canonical_interpretation.wild_to_captive_guardrail: Wild occurrence and captive diet inclusion are descriptive evidence, not a captive percentage or unlimited-feeding prescription.
